news.title: API and The Intern Group join forces to connect study abroad, internships, and career readiness
news.summary_en: Academic Programs International (API) has announced the acquisition of The Intern Group (TIG), bringing together two leading international education providers in a move designed to create more connected pathways between study abroad, international internships and graduate career readiness.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Philippines to fast-track student visas as TNE strategy takes off
news.summary_en: The Philippines will create a "green lane" for students and academics seeking visas to enter the country, cutting red tape and fast-tracking applications as part of its new transnational education (TNE) strategy.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: US midterm elections: what could change for international education?
news.summary_en: The Democrats’ win in the US midterm elections could have implications for international students studying in the US, amid Trump’s tightening of restrictions on study and post-graduate opportunities.
news.author: Jenna O'Flynn

news.title: International universities face pressure to prove value in India
news.summary_en: At AIEC, delegates said universities will need to match international credentials with local career pathways, mobility and credible partnerships.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: The graduate visa U-turn: are we rewarding outcomes or reinforcing old hierarchies?
news.summary_en: Could the UK’s Graduate Route U-turn reinforce university hierarchies? Diana Beech argues that graduate outcomes must be measured beyond prestige and geography.
news.author: Diana Beech

news.title: Canada-EU alliance to expand opportunities for students
news.summary_en: A newly announced alliance between Canada and the EU could create new opportunities for students on both sides of the Atlantic and forge closer academic ties between the two partners.
news.author: Jenna O'Flynn

news.title: Natalie Cryan, QS
news.summary_en: This week, The PIE spent five minutes with Natalie Cryan, senior vice president, Future Students at QS, to discuss embracing change and why people remain the most important part of the job.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: Five things we learned about Australian TNE at AIEC 2026
news.summary_en: From the commercial challenge to government’s role, delegates set out what it will take to build stronger offshore partnerships.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Germany’s international student push turns to retention
news.summary_en: Germany’s popularity as a study destination remains strong, but attention is shifting from growth alone to attracting the right students and helping them succeed. Panellists at The PIE Live Germany discussed how language, academic integration and a decentralised support system will shape the country’s ability to retain international talent.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: UK to raise HPI visa cap as eligibility expands to top 150 universities
news.summary_en: The UK government has announced that there will be a “proportional increase” in the current yearly cap on High Potential Individual visa applications, as the government unveils new plans to “go further in attracting the world’s best graduates”.
news.author: Jenna O'Flynn

news.title: New Zealand student experience hits record high, but work opportunities lag
news.summary_en: International student satisfaction in New Zealand has reached its highest level since national surveying began, though students continue to report difficulties finding work alongside their studies.
news.author: Kim Martin
